songs.name: I Just Want To Make Love To You

ai_show_review.summary: Rare early‑Dead cuts shine; high‑energy set with standout Big Boy Pete
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a handful of ultra‑rare early‑Dead numbers—Viola Lee Blues, The Same Thing and the first Me And My Uncle—plus an exuberant vocal trade on Big Boy Pete. Bill Kreutzmann opens with a bebop‑style drum figure that sets a lively tone. Overall performance is strong despite typical 1966 recording murkiness.
ai_show_review.review: On November 29, 1966 the Grateful Dead rolled into The Matrix with a set packed full of rarity and raw energy. From the opening bebop‑driven kick by Bill to Pigpen’s raucous lead on Big Boy Pete, the band was clearly in a creative upswing. Jerry’s voice, though hampered by a cold, handed off duties to Phil on several numbers and still managed a compelling trade with Bob during the Pigpen‑led “Big Boy Pete.” The setlist is a treasure trove for collectors – it contains the first known performance of “Me And My Uncle,” blistering renditions of “Viola Lee Blues” and “The Same Thing,” plus deep cuts like “Stealin’,” “One Kind Favor,” and “Early Morning Rain.” While early‑Dead soundboard captures often suffer from channel drop‑outs and a bit of murk, the recommended Graham‑Perlstein recording presents these moments with enough clarity to feel the historic vibe. Fans seeking both the rare repertoire and an authentic glimpse into the band’s formative stage will find this show rewarding.

best_recording.reason: Clear soundboard capture that includes the full set of rare early‑Dead cuts; only minor right‑channel dropout on Viola Lee Blues, but overall representative and listenable.

key_highlights: Ultra‑rare early repertoire (Viola Lee Blues, The Same Thing, Me And My Uncle)
Pigpen‑led Big Boy Pete with lively vocal trade between Jerry and Bob
Bill Kreutzmann’s bebop‑style drum intro that kicks off the show
High‑energy three‑set marathon preserving a historic 1966 vibe
song_highlights: I Just Want To Make Love To You

band_performance.Jerry: Slightly hoarse from a cold, handed vocal duties to Phil on some numbers but still delivered strong vocals, especially on Big Boy Pete where he traded lines with Bob.
band_performance.Phil: Supported the band on bass and stepped up for occasional lead vocals when Jerry was under the weather; solid foundation throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Joined Jerry in a spirited lyrical exchange on Pigpen's version of Big Boy Pete, adding energy to the performance.
band_performance.Billy: Opened the night with a bebop‑style drum figure that set an upbeat tone and kept the momentum high.
